title: AI/ML in Pharmacometrics: Hands-On Workshop and Regulatory Panel (PAGE 2026 Satellite)
journal_or_venue: PAGE 2026 (Population Approach Group Europe, Dubrovnik, Croatia)

content.abstract_summary: A satellite workshop organized by the ISoP AI/ML SIG at PAGE 2026 (Dubrovnik, June 2, 2026). Full-day hands-on program covering GenAI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot), neural ODEs in Julia, ML covariate selection in R (XGBoost, SHAP, UMAP), and a regulatory/industry panel (FDA, EMA). Targets practitioners with basic R/Julia skills. Positions the AI/ML SIG as the practical education hub for AI in pharmacometrics.
key_findings: The ISoP AI/ML SIG actively provides practical AI/ML education for pharmacometrics — a role MCS must not duplicate but can complement with mathematical depth
Workshop topics are explicitly practical and implementation-focused: GitHub Copilot for coding, XGBoost/SHAP for covariate analysis, NeuralODEs for model fitting
A regulatory/industry panel with FDA and EMA representatives confirms AI in pharmacometrics is now a live regulatory concern, not just a research topic
SHAP values are positioned as the primary XAI tool — consistent with the WG's need to critically evaluate SHAP limitations and address them more rigorously
GenAI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot) are highlighted as a distinct educational topic — the AI/ML SIG is claiming this space; MCS should not compete here
limitations: Workshop agenda and overview only — no research outcomes, benchmark results, or methodological depth documented
Single-day program; depth of coverage on each topic is limited by time

extracted_claims.text: The workshop covers "GenAI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot demonstrations)" and "deep compartment models and neural ODEs in Julia" — positioning the ISoP AI/ML SIG firmly in practical education rather than mathematical foundations.
Workshop frames AI/ML as "rapidly transforming pharmacometrics" by offering "new tools for model development, covariate selection, and data analysis."

gaps_addressed: Confirms the ISoP AI/ML SIG's positioning as the practical education provider — the MCS WG must differentiate by providing mathematical rigor, not duplicating this workshop content
Shows NeuralODEs and SHAP are now mainstream enough for workshop education — MCS should engage at the foundational/limitations level, not the introductory level

provenance.notes: Fetched from https://aiml-sig.github.io/2026-page-workshop/. Key strategic source for understanding what the ISoP AI/ML SIG (launched Dec 2023) is doing educationally — directly informs MCS WG differentiation strategy.
